title: Lumis: Syntax Highlighter powered by Tree-sitter
partialText: Lumis looks like a pretty sweet new syntax highlighter tool. Powered by Tree-sitter, of which I can vouch for its speed and power. I like how many runtimes it supports, almost encouraging server-side use, which is the best place for the job when you can pull it off.

title: Lessons Learned Rewriting a Sticky Detector
partialText: A dozen years go by, it turns out we can do things a lot differently and a lot better. Here a `scroll` event is entirely replaced by HTML and CSS features and much better performance.

title: FixCSS

title: In-N-Out Animation using sibling-index()
partialText: Temani mimics a View Transition by placing items using their index and translations. The placement calculation change when the index changes, which is an animation opportunity!

title: The Siren Song of ariaNotify()
partialText: Mat Marquis details the good-and-dangerous of a new method which we can just make a screenreader say something. There’s a brand new ariaNotify() method — defined by the Accessible Rich Internet Applications (WAI-ARIA) 1.3 Specification — that provides you with a means of programmatically triggering narration in a screen reader. title: Thinking Horizontally in CSS @layer
partialText: If you put your custom properties (tokens) for every component in an @layer, then overriding them is never a fight.

title: How to Make an Interactive Element Invisible but Accessible
partialText: The attribute `hidden="until-found" can be quite useful in HTML, but we'll need another unexpected bit of CSS to ensure space is reserved.

title: Boundary-Aware Styling in CSS
partialText: You might think of the view() function as used in scroll-driven animations, but really it just pairs @keyframes animation with the current position of an element.

title: The Field Guide to Grid Lanes
partialText: The WebKit gang did a good job with The Field Guide to Grid Lanes showcasing what kind of layouts are now achievable with display: grid-lanes;. Basically: Masonry layout, with arbitrary column widths, and proper tabbing order, is now progressive-enhanceable and HTML/CSS only.

title: Cloudflare Workers and Hyperdrive with TanStack Start
partialText: In Part 2 of the series on using Cloudflare with Web Apps, the focus is on setting up a database and addressing key issues like performance and connection management.
